body:
Source: GitHub issue #739 (bug, security, P1-high, area:rails). Re-verified on main @ 982adee7: packages/rails-guard/lib/rails.mjs:56, `checkRailEdits` honours `sanctionedAdditions` membership with a bare `continue` (no return value carries which files were exempted) — the function's own doc comment says this is "MECHANISM only" and the caller owns policy, which is a defensible split, but nothing downstream of it ever records the exemption. packages/rails-guard/lib/output.mjs's `buildResult` has no sanctioned-paths field; `--json` emits `railsDiffEmpty: true, passed: true` with zero trace; the human path prints only `rails-guard: all checks passed`; and bin/rails-guard.mjs:296's `--record` call hardcodes `railsDiffEmpty: true` into the manifest entry with no sanctioned-paths field either, so the evidence ledger records a clean rails-diff-empty proof for a run where railed paths were in fact exempted. The bin's own `--sanctioned-add` help text says "do not pass by hand" (documentation, not enforcement), and `packages/core/lib/shell.mjs` allowlists `adlc rails-guard` as read-only in the agent shell ladder, so an agent can already invoke it with arbitrary flags.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. Package `packages/rails-guard`: bin/rails-guard.mjs is the CLI entry (parses `--sanctioned-add` at line ~245 into a `Set`, calls `runChecks` then `buildResult`, prints human/JSON output, and on `--record` appends the manifest entry at ~line 279-300). lib/check.mjs's `runChecks({..., sanctionedAdditions})` orchestrates rail-edit + suppression checks and calls `checkRailEdits(changedFiles, railGlobs, resolveContents, sanctionedAdditions)` (lib/rails.mjs) — this is the ONLY place that currently knows which files were sanctioned, and it discards that list. lib/output.mjs's `buildResult({violations, railGlobs, railGlobError, railsDiffEmpty, suppressionsClean, base, ticket})` builds both the `--json` shape and the manifest-record shape from the same object — you are adding one field to its input/output, not changing its existing fields. lib/suppressions.mjs, lib/version-only.mjs, lib/trust-root-authorization.mjs, bin/rails-guard-ci.mjs, lib/ci/** are the STRICTER CI-side gate and unrelated — this ticket touches only the interactive `rails-guard` bin's disclosure, not rails-guard-ci.mjs's separate enforcement. Tests: `npm test -w packages/rails-guard` from the worktree root.

DO NOT rename or change the MEANING of the existing `railsDiffEmpty` field — packages/runner/lib/assertions.mjs:523-524 is a real cross-package consumer that asserts `entry.railsDiffEmpty !== true` on manifest evidence and would break on a rename or a semantic change. Implement the issue's PRIMARY recommendation (additive disclosure), not its rename alternative.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. `checkRailEdits` (lib/rails.mjs) returns BOTH the violations array AND the sanctioned matches it exempted — change its return shape from a bare `violations` array to `{violations, sanctioned}` where `sanctioned` is the array of `{file, globs}` entries for every path that matched a rail glob but was skipped via `sanctionedAdditions?.has(file)` (the `continue` at rails.mjs:56-58). The pre-existing #228 version-only exemption (rails.mjs:60-62) is NOT part of `sanctioned` — keep that skip path exactly as-is, undisclosed, since it is a different, already-accepted exemption class the issue does not ask to change.
2. Update every caller of `checkRailEdits` for the new return shape (grep the whole repo, not just lib/check.mjs — packages/core/lib/git.mjs also references it per the ticket's own consumer scan; confirm at build time whether that reference is a real call site or an unrelated mention, and fix accordingly).
3. `runChecks` (lib/check.mjs) threads the new `sanctioned` list through its return object as `sanctionedAdditions: string[]` (just the file paths, sorted, deduped — the `globs` detail from step 1 does not need to survive past this layer).
4. `buildResult` (lib/output.mjs) accepts and emits a new `sanctionedAdditions: string[]` field (empty array when nothing was exempted) alongside the existing fields — additive only, no existing field renamed or removed.
5. Human-readable output (bin/rails-guard.mjs, the `violations.length === 0` branch): when `sanctionedAdditions.length > 0`, print the sanctioned paths on STDERR (matching the existing advisory-note pattern already used for the rails-guard-ci reminder in that same branch) — stdout piping stays unaffected.
6. The `--record` manifest entry (bin/rails-guard.mjs ~line 279-300) includes the new `sanctionedAdditions` array verbatim (empty array when none) alongside the existing hardcoded `railsDiffEmpty: true`. `railsDiffEmpty`'s existing semantics and value are UNCHANGED by this ticket (still true whenever there are zero rail-edit violations, exemptions included) — this ticket makes the exemption visible in the SAME record, it does not redefine what railsDiffEmpty means.
7. Documentation: update `packages/rails-guard/README.md` and hand-edit the same statement into `docs/tools/rails-guard.md` and `apps/docs/content/docs/toolkit/rails-guard.mdx` (mirrors — never regenerate), describing the new `sanctionedAdditions` field in both `--json` output and the `--record` manifest entry.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 `checkRailEdits` returns `{violations, sanctioned}`; a call with a sanctioned file returns that file (with its matched globs) in `sanctioned` and nothing for it in `violations`; a call with no sanctionedAdditions passed behaves exactly as before (empty `sanctioned`, same `violations`). verify: `node --test packages/rails-guard/test/rails.test.mjs`
- AC2 `runChecks` output includes `sanctionedAdditions: [<file>]` when a sanctioned rail match occurred, `[]` otherwise; `railsDiffEmpty` computation is unchanged (still true whenever there are zero rail-edit violations, sanctioned or version-only-exempted files included, exactly as today). verify: `node --test packages/rails-guard/test/check.test.mjs`
- AC3 `--json` CLI output on a `--sanctioned-add`-exempted run includes a non-empty `sanctionedAdditions` array naming the exempted file(s); on an ordinary clean run (no exemptions used) it is `[]`. verify: `node --test packages/rails-guard/test/ci-bin.test.mjs` or a new `packages/rails-guard/test/sanctioned-disclosure.test.mjs` if the CLI-level case does not already have a natural home
- AC4 `--record` on a `--sanctioned-add`-exempted clean run appends a manifest entry whose `sanctionedAdditions` array names the exempted file(s), alongside the unchanged `railsDiffEmpty: true`. verify: `node --test packages/rails-guard/test/record.test.mjs`
- AC5 `packages/runner/lib/assertions.mjs`'s `railsDiffEmpty !== true` check is unaffected — its consumer test still passes unmodified. verify: `npm test -w packages/runner` (or `node --test packages/runner/test/*.test.mjs` if there is no npm script)
- AC6 Existing suite green (rails.test.mjs, check.test.mjs, rail-addition-sanction.test.mjs, record.test.mjs, ci-bin.test.mjs and the rest) — rail-addition-sanction.test.mjs in particular already exercises `--sanctioned-add`; if it asserts on the OLD `checkRailEdits` return shape (bare array) it must be updated for the new `{violations, sanctioned}` shape, and say so in the PR body. verify: `npm test -w packages/rails-guard`
- AC7 Docs updated in all three places. verify: `grep -c "sanctionedAdditions" packages/rails-guard/README.md docs/tools/rails-guard.md apps/docs/content/docs/toolkit/rails-guard.mdx` (each >= 1)
- AC8 Mutation gate green on the branch. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally before review)

OUT OF SCOPE: bin/rails-guard-ci.mjs and lib/ci/** (the stricter, separately-owned CI gate — this ticket is the interactive bin only); the #228 version-only exemption's own disclosure (unchanged, pre-existing, not part of this issue); renaming `railsDiffEmpty` (explicitly rejected above — would break packages/runner's consumer); enforcing that `--sanctioned-add` may only be passed by a trusted caller (out of scope per the issue itself — "not a NEW hole in the bin's threat model").
title: rails-guard: disclose --sanctioned-add exemptions in --json output and the --record manifest entry
